full_judgment: 5. Leave was granted to consider the submission that the High Court Division acted illegally in making the Rule absolute on consideration that the respondent No.3 does not have the authority under section 11(2) of the Companies Act to issue such direction for changing the name of the respondent No.1 company so long as section 11(2) of the said Act only speaks of a registration with identical name with a company in existence and further submission that the High Court Division acted illegally in holding that since the respondent No. 1 company obtained certificate on 10.10.2001 from the respondent No. 3 pursuant to section 11(6) of the Companies Act, 1994 and as such any subsequent action by the respondent No. 3 is without lawful authority and if such person is aggrieved by the change of name under section 11(6) of the said Act, he can take steps against such change in accordance with law and the further submission that the High Court Division acted illegally in not considering the fraud and forgery committed by the respondent No.1 Company in obtaining the said certificate for changing the said name from the respondent No. 3 and the respondent No.1 company has not come before this Court with clean hand and more so the High Court Division totally ignored the Investigation Report of the respondent No. 3 dated 18.08.2003 and virtually opened the floodgate for forgery and fraud and the further submission that the High Court Division failed to consider that there is no illegality in the said memo dated 09.07.2003 so long as the scope of section (2) of the said .Act is wide enough To give such direction, to respondent No.1 company and if such order is passed under section 11(2) of the said Act, the likelihood of deception can be inferred through necessary implication or presumption.
